Dashboard working! Cross-compiled Bevy exe launches from WSL via cmd.exe /C start with Stdio::null() — fully detaches from WSL fds, no more read failed 5 errors. User confirmed window is visible on Windows desktop with 3D graph rendering.

Architecture: Legend has three memory layers — immediate buffer (FIFO, 256 cap), short-term vector store (cosine similarity, salience decay, 1024 cap), and long-term knowledge graph (Hebbian reinforcement, 2048 nodes, 8192 edges). Data flows upward: tick writes to immediate+short-term, consolidate merges into graph.

Key source files: src/memory/mod.rs is the core engine (MemoryState, tick, retrieve_context, consolidate, prune). src/memory/embed.rs handles n-gram embeddings and cosine similarity. src/memory/extract.rs does code-aware entity extraction. src/memory/summarize.rs does extractive summarization with decision-rationale boosting.

Decision: chose Bevy over egui-only because we wanted true 3D force-directed graph with orbit camera, not just flat 2D panels. Bevy gives us PBR materials with emissive glow for salience, gizmo lines for edges, and proper 3D transforms for node positioning.

User preference: wants native app, not web UI. WSL environment means cross-compiling to Windows exe via x86_64-pc-windows-gnu target with mingw linker. Launch via cmd.exe /C start to avoid fd inheritance issues.
